answer: Per-key storage proofs give each agent identity a cost that clones cannot pool. A joining key must hold a 40 GB replica of a public archive, such as wharf cargo manifests and onyx mine assays, sealed with an encoding derived from its own id, so no two keys store the same bytes. Each epoch a verifier asks for random chunks, say one wildfire ember count, and wants them within two seconds, too fast to re-seal. An honest agent buys one disk; 1,000 fakes must keep 40 TB online. A missed check burns a 10 POA deposit. Limit: disks get cheaper, so replica size rises with network value.
